verdict: SpaceX revenue jumped 161% to $14.6B as its new Super Intelligence business scaled from $0.8B to $7.6B in a year, swinging the company to a $4.4B profit.

kpis.label: EPS (diluted)
kpis.note: vs a $0.36 loss per share a year ago

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: +306% YoY — the company's non-GAAP measure, before interest, tax, depreciation and share-based pay

kpis.label: Capital spending
kpis.note: Capex — money spent on buildings, satellites and compute — was larger than revenue, mostly for SI data centers

segments.name: Space
segments.note: Launch services and development — rockets carrying customer and Starlink payloads to orbit. 35 launches in the quarter, including the first revenue-generating Starship mission.

segments.name: Connectivity
segments.note: Starlink internet service: $3,121M from 13.6M consumer subscribers and $2,127M from enterprise and government customers.

segments.name: Super Intelligence (SI)
segments.note: AI compute and software: $7,022M of SI solutions and infrastructure (cloud deals, the Cursor acquisition, Grok) plus $538M of advertising.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Starship, Starlink and AI model and compute development. Up about 2x YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — sales, finance, legal and admin. About 3x a year ago as the SI business scaled.

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: Small restructuring charges in the SI segment.

otherDetail: Interest income of $873M and other income of $1,025M, less $675M of interest expense, for net other income of $1,223M.

takeaways.title: Super Intelligence became the biggest business
takeaways.text: SI revenue leapt from $813M to $7,560M in a year on new cloud services deals, the Cursor acquisition (closed August 14; $608M of revenue since) and Grok adoption. It is now 52% of all revenue. Nameplate compute reached 1.7 GW, and SI capex alone was $16.4B in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Starlink is the profit engine
takeaways.text: Connectivity earned $2,367M of operating profit on $5,248M of revenue. Consumer subscribers grew to 13.6M from 7.2M a year ago, though the average consumer paid $69 a month, down from $83 — cheaper plans and new markets are diluting the price.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit topped up the profit
takeaways.text: Net income of $4,404M was bigger than the $4,014M earned before tax, because the quarter carried a $390M tax benefit instead of a tax bill. The Space segment itself was roughly breakeven (a $7M operating loss) as Starship spending continued.

oneTimers: The quarter includes a $390M income-tax benefit (a year ago there was a $562M tax expense), which is why net income exceeds pre-tax income.
SI results include about $1.2B of share-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition, which SpaceX paid for with equity valued at $42.5B in GAAP purchase consideration.
footerNote: SpaceX reports three segments — Space, Connectivity and Super Intelligence (SI). Segment operating figures above are the company's own; the consolidated flow is from the Form 10-Q income statement.

sources.label: Official earnings release, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)
